transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I guess… what brings me in is that I feel like I can’t really settle in my own body anymore. Like if I’m supposed to sit down quietly and do paperwork, or go over household plans with someone, I just feel this restlessness, like I need to get up or move or something.

It’s frustrating because it sounds so simple—just sit and handle things—but it feels like my body won’t cooperate. And then I end up thinking about other little things around the house, like, oh, that drawer needs sorting, or I should move the laundry, and then I’m not really doing the thing I sat down to do.
Do you find yourself feeling unusually worried or anxious, especially when you're trying to sit still or focus on something?

I don’t know if I’d call it anxious exactly. I mean, sometimes I get tense because I know I’m supposed to be focusing, and then I’m not, and then I start thinking, “Why can’t I just do this?” But it’s not always worry, if that makes sense.

It’s more like… my brain is looking for the next thing, or my body wants to move. Like yesterday I sat down to look at something and suddenly noticed the plant needed water, and then I remembered the recycling, and then—sorry, that’s probably not what you asked. I guess I’m not sure it feels like anxiety so much as just being unsettled.
Do you often find yourself moving, fidgeting, or talking more than usual, especially when you're trying to stay still or quiet?

Yeah, I do. Not always talking more, I guess, but the moving part, definitely. Like in church meetings or family dinners, I’m usually twisting my wedding ring, or bouncing my foot under the table, or shifting around in the chair.

I try really hard to look like I’m sitting normally, especially at dinner because everyone’s just… you know, having a normal conversation, passing dishes, and I don’t want to seem rude. But my hands are doing something almost the whole time. Sometimes I don’t even notice until I’ve been spinning my ring for ages.
Do you find it hard to stay focused on tasks or conversations, even when there’s nothing else going on around you?

Yeah, I do. Even if it’s quiet, like there’s no TV on or nobody interrupting me, I can sit down with a planning email or a chapter of a book and start out okay. And then a few minutes later I realize I’m just staring at the same paragraph and none of it actually went in.

It’s embarrassing sometimes, because I’ll think, “Wait, did I read this already?” and then I go back, and then somehow I’m still not absorbing it. It’s like my eyes are doing the reading but my brain has wandered off somewhere else.
Do you often feel like you need to finish things quickly or jump into activities without thinking them through first, like you're acting on impulse?

Yeah… I think so, but more in conversations than like, running off to do some big activity. I really do care about being respectful, and I don’t want to be the person who cuts people off.

But with my husband especially, if he’s telling me something, I’ll jump in before he’s done because I already think I know where he’s going. Or I’ll finish his sentence, and then he’ll kind of look at me like, “Can I finish?” And I feel bad immediately.

It’s like the response is right there and it comes out before I’ve made myself wait. I don’t mean to be rude. I’m trying to listen, but then I’m also… already answering in my head, if that makes sense.
Looking back, did you have similar experiences with restlessness, trouble focusing, or acting impulsively when you were a child, like in school or at home?

Yeah, looking back, I think it was there pretty early. Like elementary school early.

I was always the kid with the disaster desk, papers shoved in there, permission slips missing until the last second—or my mom would find them crumpled in my backpack after the thing already happened. And I remember teachers sending notes home about me talking when I wasn’t supposed to, or not staying in my seat.

It’s funny, I can picture those little desks with the metal legs, and I had this one pencil box I loved—sorry, that’s not really the point. But yes, it wasn’t just an adult thing. I think I just didn’t have words for it then.
